analysis.investment_thesis: CreditAccess Grameen has a strong promoter (66.28%), meaningful scale, and an admirable mission serving rural women — but the MFI sector is in severe industry-wide stress, net profit collapsed 63% from INR 1,446 Cr (FY24) to INR 531 Cr (FY25), and the inherent leverage of 2.81x D/E combined with regulatory/political risk makes this unsuitable for my concentrated, conservative portfolio today.
key_strengths: Promoter holding of 66.28% is excellent — highest skin-in-the-game among all five stocks reviewed
Revenue CAGR of 28.4% over 6 years demonstrates strong growth engine and rural penetration capability
Forward P/E of 13.65x suggests the market is pricing in earnings recovery — if MFI stress normalises, the risk-reward improves
key_risks: Net profit collapsed 63% YoY (INR 1,446 Cr → INR 531 Cr in FY25) — this is not a one-quarter blip but a sector-wide credit cycle turning
MFI sector is structurally vulnerable to loan waivers, political interference, and borrower over-indebtedness — risks that are intensifying right now
ROE of 7.86% is well below my 15% threshold; the company is barely covering its cost of equity at current profitability levels
red_flags: Total assets declined from INR 28,871 Cr (FY24) to INR 27,679 Cr (FY25) — loan book shrinking is the clearest signal of asset quality stress and collections pressure
OCF was positive in only 1 of the last 5 years (the 2025 positive is driven by loan book contraction, not genuine operational improvement)
Finance costs growing relentlessly — INR 417 Cr (FY19) to INR 1,955 Cr (FY25), a 4.7x increase, as the liability franchise scales up cost
analysis.detailed_analysis: I respect the microfinance mission and the strong promoter backing, but I have seen enough business cycles to know that lending to the most financially fragile segment of society is a uniquely risky business when the cycle turns. The FY25 numbers confirm the turn has arrived: net profit down 63%, total loan book shrinking, ROE below 8%, and negative OCF in four of the past five years. The forward P/E of 13.65x is tempting but reflects consensus hopes for recovery — I would rather wait to see two clear quarters of improving asset quality metrics before considering entry, and even then this would not be a large position for me.
